html:
A holy war launched around 1725 by Muslim Fula (Fulbe) herders in the Futa Jallon highlands of what is now Guinea. Led by the cleric Karamokho Alfa, they overthrew the non-Muslim rulers of the area and set up the Imamate of Futa Jallon, a state run under Islamic law with its capital at Timbo. Power alternated between two leading families.

It was the first of a chain of Islamic revolutions in West Africa led by Fula scholars:

  • Futa Toro, on the Senegal river, in 1776.
  • The Sokoto Caliphate of Usman dan Fodio, from 1804.
  • The Massina state on the inland Niger delta, from 1818.
  • The Toucouleur Empire of Umar Tall, from the 1850s.

Futa Jallon became a centre of Muslim learning. It also raided and traded in enslaved people, many sold to European ships on the coast. France made it a protectorate in 1896.
